paragraphs: Abba Shaul son of Imi Miriam, Ketubot 87a. Hyman identifies this as a woman’s name, citing Tosafot on Bava Batra 149a, s.v. Rav Mari.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Imi Miriam is explicitly described as a woman’s name.

The whole Davidson Ketubot 87a paragraphs write Abba Shaul ben Imma Miriam, while Hyman supplies Imi Miriam. The whole digital Vilna Tosafot Bava Batra 149a paragraph beginning Rav Mari discusses naming a person after his mother and includes Abba Shaul ben Imma Miriam among its comparisons. That supports the context of Hyman’s woman’s-name statement, without importing the other people’s genealogies, asserting a printed-page collation, or harmonizing Imi/Imma forms.
